title: A scene with a SubViewport with WorldEnvironment/DirectionalLight3D and own_world_3d=true disables default lighting/enviornment in editor
body:
### Tested versions

Probably reproducible since whenever this default light/env feature existed, I'm on 4.6.

### System information

N/A

### Issue description

Technically not a bug, but the behavior does not make a whole lot of sense. own_world_3d=true makes it so the world environment/directional light do NOT get used outside of the viewport, So does not make sense to not let the preview lighting/env work. This is also recursive so for every scene this viewport exists in sub-scenes, if it doesnt have its own env/directional light this will make that scene very hard to see and edit.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68c8d1d3-4bfc-4072-b8e4-e0e8d8fdc442

This behavior can be somewhat fixed with custom `@tool` scripts but its a bit hacky. If there is a different solution that does not involve that let me know, I could not find a solution by just regular editor fiddling. 
### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new `Node3D` scene and a reference mesh(to see affected by light/env).
2. Add a `SubViewport` Node.
3. In the `SubViewport`, add a `WorldEnvironment` and/or `DirectionalLight3D` node/s.
4. The preview lighting/env is now disabled. The scene lighting looks very dark and it is very hard to edit and see objects.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30143525/test.zip)
